tool.name: FillCorridorHoles

summary.para:
View online help files: https://www.jennessent.com/corridor-designer-tools/fill-corridor-holes.html
Closes small interior holes in one or more polygon feature classes -- typically a Least-Cost Corridor output, but works on any polygon dataset. Every hole (interior ring) smaller than a size threshold is filled; holes at or above the threshold are left as real, meaningful gaps such as a lake or a genuinely excluded area. Hole size is measured as true geodesic area, correct on any coordinate system including a geographic one. Every attribute field is preserved unchanged; only the geometry is edited.

tool.usage:
A modernized port of the original CorridorDesigner Python toolbox's "Fill holes in corridor" tool. The original used a positive/negative buffer trick to morphologically close narrow gaps -- effective, but it only ever closes gaps up to roughly twice the buffer distance, has no real size control, and the original tool checked for the Spatial Analyst extension even though it never actually used it. This version instead measures every hole directly and gives an exact, unit-of-your-choice size threshold.
Fill small, keep large. Holes smaller than the threshold are filled (removed); holes at or above the threshold are left alone. This is the standard, useful direction for a hole-cleanup tool -- it cleans up small rasterization artifacts and slivers while preserving genuinely large, meaningful gaps (a lake in the middle of a habitat polygon, a real excluded area) -- and it matches the only direction Esri's own Eliminate Polygon Part tool supports.
Not Esri's Eliminate Polygon Part. That tool was tested directly against this need and rejected: its area threshold is planar only, and on a geographic (latitude/longitude) coordinate system it does not correctly convert an areal-unit string at all -- in testing, a 50,000 square meter threshold eliminated a real 111,000 square meter hole outright, silently, with no error. Least-Cost Corridor output, the primary input this tool targets, is very often geographic. This tool instead measures every hole's true geodesic area directly, exact on any coordinate system, projected or geographic, and reconstructs the geometry from Esri's own ring/hole grouping (each polygon's own geo-interface structure) rather than hand-guessing which rings are exterior boundaries and which are holes.
Multiple inputs in one run. Every polygon feature class listed is processed independently and written to its own output -- named "<input base name><name suffix>" (default suffix "_holes_removed") in the output workspace. Every attribute field from the source is preserved exactly; a straight schema copy, with only the geometry edited where a hole qualified for removal. A non-polygon input is skipped with a warning rather than failing the whole run.
Metadata chaining. When an input already carries a Land Facet linkage record -- most commonly a Least-Cost Corridor output -- the same record (same kind, same analysis id) is stamped on the output, with a note appended describing this step (the threshold, the units, how many holes were removed). The Corridor Analysis Data Report keeps describing the output as the same analysis product, now also noting it was hole-cleaned. An input with no linkage record gets none on the output either -- there is nothing to chain from, and none is invented.
Needs no Spatial Analyst.

dialogReference.para: One or more polygon feature classes to process. Each gets its own independent output; a non-polygon input is skipped with a warning rather than stopping the run.

param.name: threshold_value
param.displayname: Hole size threshold (holes smaller than this are filled)

dialogReference.para: Holes with a true geodesic area smaller than this value are filled; holes at or above it are left alone. Must be greater than zero.

The unit the threshold value above is given in: Square Meters, Hectares, Square Kilometers, Square Feet, Acres, or Square Miles. Converted internally to square meters, the unit every hole's geodesic area is measured in, so this works correctly regardless of the input's own coordinate system or units.
Where every output feature class is written. Defaults to the first input's own workspace.
Appended to each input's base name to form its output name, e.g. "Facet_Corridors" with the default suffix becomes "Facet_Corridors_holes_removed".
The hole-filled outputs, one per input processed (skipped inputs are not represented here).

scriptExample.title: Fill Corridor Holes example (stand-alone script)
scriptExample.para: Cleans small holes (under 5,000 square meters) from two Least-Cost Corridor outputs in one run.
scriptExample.code:
import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your installed path is shown in this tool's run messages
arcpy.jenness.FillCorridorHoles( [r"C:\data\out.gdb\Facet_Corridors", r"C:\data\out.gdb\Species_Corridor"], 5000, "Square Meters", r"C:\data\out.gdb", "_holes_removed")

dataIdInfo.idCredit: Jeff Jenness, Dan Majka and Paul Beier, from the CorridorDesigner toolkit (corridordesign.org). A modernized port of the CorridorDesigner toolbox's Fill Holes in Corridor tool, replacing its buffer trick with an exact geodesic hole-size threshold.
